excerpt: The Group’s TCB solutions gained further traction with multiple customers and major AI players during the year and delivered record yearly revenue and bookings in 2024. The breakthrough in High Bandwidth Memory (“HBM”) led to a significant growth in overall bookings for TCB YoY.
scope_note: COMPARATOR ROW. The incumbent's own dating of when HBM entered its TCB order book: 2024. A bookings claim, not revenue -- bookings are orders taken, which the issuer reports separately from revenue and which may be delivered over several later periods. No customer, tool count or value is attached to the HBM portion.
notes: W13 RECORDS REVIEW (accept) by claude_w13_records_verifier: Confirmed against asmpt_annual_2024 p.14: "The breakthrough in High Bandwidth Memory ('HBM') led to a significant growth in overall bookings for TCB YoY" matches verbatim. link_kind supplier_capability is a reasonable, conservative tier for a bookings/order-intake claim (bookings are orders, not confirmed production use); application_id hbm is directly supported by the named term.

excerpt: The Group is the current TCB market leader with record TCB revenue and bookings in 2024. TCB TAM growth will be driven by both logic and increasingly HBM applications. ASMPT is a market leader in Logic applications, and had a breakthrough into the HBM market with a Q4 2024 bulk order. The Group is also currently in substantive engagement with HBM players.
scope_note: COMPARATOR ROW, and the sharpest date in the set: a Q4 2024 bulk order is the issuer's stated breakthrough into HBM TCB, with other HBM customers only at 'substantive engagement'. Deliberately NOT registered from this passage: the TCB total-addressable-market figures and the 35-40% share target on the same page, which are market sizing and a target, both reference tier. The self-description as market leader is the issuer's own and is not independently established here.
notes: W13 RECORDS REVIEW (correct) by claude_w13_records_verifier: Confirmed against asmpt_annual_2024 p.15: "ASMPT...had a breakthrough into the HBM market with a Q4 2024 bulk order" matches verbatim. TIER DEFECT: filed at production_claim, but the substantive HBM-specific claim here is a BULK ORDER -- booked, not confirmed delivered, qualified or in production use. This is internally inconsistent with the sibling link asmpt_hbm_hybrid_bonder_maiden_orders_2024 in the same filing, which describes the same kind of fact (orders secured in 2024, not yet delivered) and is correctly filed at the weaker supplier_capability, explicitly reasoning 'orders, not deliveries.' An order is not production use or qualification under the protocol's own NAURA calibration ('应用于先进封装...的量产'). Downgrading to supplier_capability makes this link consistent with its sibling and with the verb actually used ('had a breakthrough...with a...bulk order', not a shipped/delivered/qualified claim). The TAM and 35-40% share-target figures on the same page are correctly excluded from this link as reference-tier, which is sound and unaffected by this correction.

excerpt: The Group achieved a major milestone in Q3 2024 with the delivery of its first HB tool to a logic customer. During the year, the Group also secured maiden orders for two next generation HB tools for HBM applications. These tools are set for delivery by mid-2025 and have enhanced capabilities, such as improved placement accuracy, reduced bonding pitch, significantly higher throughput, and a more compact tool footprint.
scope_note: COMPARATOR ROW. Maiden orders for two next-generation hybrid bonders for HBM, ordered in 2024 for delivery by mid-2025 -- orders, not deliveries, and the first HB tool actually delivered in 2024 went to a LOGIC customer, not an HBM one. Filed at the bonding parent rather than a hybrid child because the source does not say whether these are wafer-to-wafer or die-to-wafer tools, and HBM hybrid bonding is usually die-to-wafer only by inference, which is not evidence.
notes: W13 RECORDS REVIEW (accept) by claude_w13_records_verifier: Confirmed against asmpt_annual_2024 p.15: "the Group also secured maiden orders for two next generation HB tools for HBM applications. These tools are set for delivery by mid-2025" matches verbatim. link_kind supplier_capability correctly reflects that these are orders for future delivery, not deliveries; the scope_note honestly notes the first HB tool actually delivered in 2024 went to a LOGIC customer, not an HBM one. Category 'bonding' parent is correct since the source does not state wafer-to-wafer vs die-to-wafer mechanism.

excerpt: Driven by artificial intelligence (“AI”), the Group recorded revenue of US$532.1 million for its advanced packaging (“AP”) business. This was up 30.2% YoY, with a significant contribution from its Thermo-Compression Bonding (“TCB”) solutions.
scope_note: COMPARATOR ROW carrying the one published advanced-packaging revenue figure in this step: US$532.1m in FY2025, up 30.2%, which the issuer attributes substantially to TCB. 'Significant contribution' is not a split, so no part of the figure may be assigned to TCB alone. Registered against advanced_packaging rather than hbm because the sentence names AI broadly, not HBM.
notes: W13 RECORDS REVIEW (accept) by claude_w13_records_verifier: Confirmed against asmpt_annual_2025 p.13: "the Group recorded revenue of US$532.1 million for its advanced packaging ('AP') business...with a significant contribution from its...TCB...solutions" matches verbatim. link_kind production_claim correct (this is realized revenue, not an order or capability claim). application_id advanced_packaging (not hbm) correct since the sentence names AI broadly, not HBM. Scope_note correctly states 'significant contribution' is not a split and no TCB-only figure can be extracted from it.
